notes.enva: Dek is any sauce eaten with kwon.

guidebook.intro: Food in Acholi land means **kwon** (a stiff bread of millet or cassava) with **dek** (sauce). Learn to say you are hungry and to buy at the **cuk** (market).

tips.title: Hunger is killing me
body: Acholi says hunger and thirst grip you: **Kec tye ka nekka** (I’m hungry, literally “hunger is killing me”), **Orio tye ka nekka** (I’m thirsty).
To have is to be with: **Atye ki** (I have), **Itye ki** (you have), **Pe atye ki** (I don’t have).

tips.title: Tye ka: doing it now
body: **Atye ka** plus a verb is “I am …ing”: **Atye ka wilo matoke** (I am buying matooke). The plain form **Awilo** is “I buy”.

culture.title: Kwon and dek
body: A meal is **kwon** with a **dek**: beans, groundnut paste, smoked fish, or **malakwang**, a sour leafy sauce that is a favourite in Acholi homes. Guests are always offered food, and saying **Mit matek!** (it’s very tasty) is the best thanks.
